annotations.title: Show how prices at a development or area moved over time

description: Use this when a user asks how prices at a Singapore development, HDB town or postal district have moved over time, such as "How have prices at The Sail moved since 2020?" or "How have HDB prices in Tampines moved?", or wants the price trends of up to 4 of them side by side. Give each subject exactly one of: project (a private condo or apartment project, such as "The Sail"), hdbStreet (an HDB street, such as "Tampines St 81"), hdbTown (an HDB town, such as "Tampines" or "Kallang/Whampoa", for every HDB resale there), postalDistrict (1 to 28, for the private strata homes such as condos and apartments in that district), or street with homes "landed" for the landed homes on that street, or street with homes "non_landed" and its district for the apartments there without a project name. An hdbStreet or hdbTown subject without flatType mixes every flat type, so each quarter's median moves with its mix of flat sizes; when the user owns, sells or wants one flat type, such as a 4-room flat, give flatType "4 ROOM" to count only that type. years counts back whole years of quarters, ending with the current quarter (default 5, up to 10); for "since 2020", pass the current year minus 2019. Returns, for each quarter with sales, the number of sales, median price and median S$ psf, marking a quarter with fewer than 3 sales as thin and the current, unfinished quarter as partial, with the Homejourney page whose chart shows the same quarters. A project name that is not a URA name resolves to the one project containing it, or nameMatch lists the candidates. Cite the page. Use get_development_transactions for the individual sales and get_development_price_summaries to compare the latest 12 months across many developments.

flatType.description: With hdbStreet or hdbTown only: one HDB flat type (1 ROOM, 2 ROOM, 3 ROOM, 4 ROOM, 5 ROOM, EXECUTIVE, MULTI-GENERATION; "4-room" also reads 4 ROOM). Without it, the medians mix every flat type.

name: get_price_trend

replyText.description: This reply as text: what it found, the next step, and every id or link a follow-up call needs. Read it before answering the user.
